transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Um… I guess I’m here because work has been getting to me more than I’d like to admit. We got a new operations manager, and he’s been picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years. I’m sure he’s just trying to do his job, but I can’t seem to leave it at work anymore.

I come home all wound up, and I’ve been snapping at my husband, which I don’t like. Then I lie awake replaying meetings in my head, and the next day I find myself second-guessing routine quality calls I used to make without any trouble. It feels silly saying it out loud, but… it’s starting to affect me.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot even when there isn't a specific problem at work or home, like feeling anxious for no clear reason?

I don’t think so… not in a general way, at least. I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m anxious for no reason all the time or anything like that. It seems more tied to when I start thinking about work, or something reminds me of it.

I hope that makes sense. It’s not like I’m just worried out of nowhere all day.
Have you noticed feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even when work isn’t on your mind?

Um… I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I have days where I feel kind of worn out or not as cheerful, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in things in general.

If I’m not thinking about work, I can still enjoy normal things. At least… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it.
Do you find it hard to control your worry about things beyond work, like everyday responsibilities or other life events, even when they’re not urgent?

I don’t think so… I mean, everyday things can feel irritating or a little heavier when I’m already stressed, but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around worrying about bills or chores or family things for no real reason.

It’s mostly when something connects back to work. At least, that’s how it seems to me. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you noticed any physical symptoms lately, like restlessness, trouble relaxing, or muscle tension, especially when you're thinking about work?

Yes… I guess I do get kind of wound up. I don’t know if I’d call it a major physical thing, but when I’m thinking about work—especially after meetings with the new operations manager picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years—I have a hard time settling down.

I come home still tense, and I’ll replay things in my head. Sometimes I’m short with my husband, which I don’t like admitting. And then the next day I’ll second-guess routine quality calls that I used to make without much trouble. So… yes, I suppose trouble relaxing fits, mostly when it’s tied to work.
Outside of work-related concerns, do you find it difficult to control worry or feel anxious about other aspects of your life, even minor things?

Not really, no. I mean, I can get annoyed or a little tense about normal life things, but I don’t feel like I’m worrying all the time about everything.

It’s mostly tied to work. If something isn’t connected to that, I can usually let it go. At least, that’s how it seems to me. Is that what you’re asking?
Have you noticed feeling unusually tired or low on energy even when things at work aren't particularly stressful?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed that, honestly. I mean, I get tired like anyone does, but I can’t say it feels unusual when work isn’t stressful.

If work is calmer, my energy seems more normal, I think. I don’t want to overstate it. Does that make sense?
Have you had trouble falling asleep or staying asleep because you're worrying about work, even when there isn't an urgent issue to resolve?

Yes… that has been happening some. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m up all night every night, but I do lie there replaying meetings in my head, especially the ones where the new operations manager was picking apart my inspection procedures.

Even if there isn’t anything I can actually fix right then, I’ll still be thinking about what I said, or whether I missed something, and then the next day I find myself second-guessing routine quality calls I used to make without much trouble. So yes, I guess work has been following me home more than I’d like.
Would you say your worry about work is more intense or lasts longer than you feel it should, even when you know the situation may not be that serious?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t always want to admit that, because part of me thinks I should be able to just brush it off.

But since the new operations manager started picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years, it’s like I can’t quite leave it at work. I come home still wound up about it, and I’ll keep going over what happened even when I know, logically, it probably isn’t some huge crisis.

It feels stronger than it should, I guess. And it lasts longer than I’d like. Does that sound like what you mean?

Even when you’re not thinking about work, do you ever find yourself feeling anxious or worried about other things in your life, like personal relationships, health, or other matters, even if they don’t seem like big issues?

I don’t think so… not in the same way. I mean, everyone worries about family or health things here and there, but I can’t say I’ve noticed myself getting anxious over little things generally.

It really seems more tied to work, at least from what I can tell. I hope that answers what you’re asking.
When you say you feel worn out or not as cheerful, do you ever have days where you feel down or lose pleasure in activities you normally enjoy, even when work isn’t on your mind?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way, exactly. I mean, I do feel kind of worn down sometimes, and maybe not as upbeat as I usually am, but I haven’t really noticed whole days where I just don’t enjoy things when work isn’t in the back of my mind.

It feels more like… if work is bothering me, it colors everything a bit. But if I’m not thinking about it, I can usually still enjoy things. I hope that makes sense.
Do you ever feel anxious or notice physical symptoms like a racing heart or stomach discomfort when thinking about things other than work, even minor concerns?

Not really, no… at least I haven’t noticed that happening with other things.

If it’s something minor at home or health-related, I don’t usually get that same anxious feeling or physical reaction. The racing heart or stomach upset—if I get anything like that—it seems to be when I’m thinking about work. I don’t want to overstate it, though. Does that answer it okay?

Do you ever feel anxious or notice physical symptoms like a racing heart or stomach discomfort when you're anticipating something work-related, like the start of the workday or an upcoming meeting with the operations manager?

Yes… I think that’s when it shows up the most, honestly. Like before the workday starts, or if I know there’s going to be a meeting with the operations manager, I get pretty wound up.

I try not to make too much of it, because I know everyone has work stress, but since he started picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years, I have a hard time just leaving it there. I’ll come home still tense, and then I’m replaying what was said or second-guessing routine quality calls I used to make without much trouble.

So… yes, anticipating work things does set it off. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Do you ever feel anxious or notice physical symptoms like a racing heart or stomach discomfort when anticipating minor events that aren't work-related, like a social gathering or a routine appointment?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, if it’s just something like a routine appointment or seeing people socially, I might think about it a little, but I don’t get that same anxious feeling in my body.

At least, not that I’ve really noticed. It seems much more tied to work situations. Does that answer what you’re asking?
